risks.title: Dependence on a limited number of aircraft manufacturers
risks.summary: AerCap relies heavily on a few manufacturers such as Boeing and Airbus. Any delivery delays due to supply chain issues, strikes, or quality defects can delay aircraft entry into service and impact leasing revenues.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is prominently mentioned in the 10-K, with strong language ("rely on a small number of manufacturers"). The trend is stable, but supply shortages and supply chain issues persist. This category weighs heavily on AerCap's business model.

risks.title: Increased competition in aircraft leasing
risks.summary: The aircraft leasing market is highly competitive. Industry consolidation, new market entrants, or strategic shifts by competitors may reduce margins and limit access to high-quality customers.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is clearly identified in the 10-K with assertive language ("significant competition"). The trend is stable, but the sector continues to attract new entrants. Competition directly affects leasing rates and placement capacity.

risks.title: Growing environmental regulation
risks.summary: Climate-related regulations, carbon emissions standards, and aircraft energy efficiency requirements are tightening. This may devalue older aircraft and force AerCap to accelerate fleet renewal.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is well positioned in the document, with concerned language ("may be supplemented by additional regulations"). The trend is upward, linked to ESG pressures. It affects the future value of assets.

risks.title: Cybersecurity of information systems
risks.summary: AerCap depends on internal and third-party IT systems to manage contracts, assets, and payments. A cyberattack could disrupt operations, compromise sensitive data, or damage its reputation.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly cited with alert language ("damaged or interrupted, including by cyberattack"). The trend is rising. Critical systems depend on digital continuity.

risks.title: Adoption of artificial intelligence
risks.summary: Integrating AI into asset or risk management exposes AerCap to operational errors, algorithmic bias, or privacy breaches, with potential regulatory or reputational consequences.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned in a dedicated section, with cautious language ("may result in operational errors"). The trend is rising. It is an emerging risk related to digital transformation.

risks.title: Increased regulation on trade and sanctions
risks.summary: Trade regulations, international sanctions (e.g., Russia, Ukraine), and customs barriers may prevent aircraft repositioning, block payments, or force market exits, directly impacting revenues.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is strongly emphasized, particularly with sanctions related to the Ukraine conflict. Intense language and strategic placement in the document. Trend is rising amid tense geopolitical conditions.

risks.title: Maintenance and insurance by lessees
risks.summary: During leases, airlines are responsible for aircraft maintenance and insurance. Poor maintenance can degrade asset value and lead to unexpected costs for AerCap upon aircraft return.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is clearly stated with language of dependency ("depend on our lessees to properly maintain"). Trend is stable. It directly affects asset integrity and future costs.

ai_positioning.summary: AerCap does not mention any initiatives related to artificial intelligence in its recent financial reports. The company focuses on its traditional aircraft leasing activities.
evidence: No mention of AI in the 10-K
No references to innovative technology projects
Absence of AI-related KPIs or strategy
